claims.text: A synergistic effect of lattice distortion and magnetic-moment localization governs the strong magnetocaloric response of rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Lattice distortion and magnetic-moment localization enhance magnetic entropy change at applied fields below 2 T.
The proposed mechanism maintains rapid heat exchange.
The proposed mechanism maintains low hysteresis.
The proposed mechanism maintains mechanical stability.
The initial material is a rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has a disordered lattice structure.
Alloy-composition modification can controllably introduce different levels of lattice distortion.
The hypothesized behavior is intended to apply at magnetic fields below 2 T.
The hypothesized behavior is intended to apply from 250 to 350 K.
Increasing lattice distortion relative to an undistorted baseline will increase magnetic entropy change.
The modified alloy will retain rapid heat exchange relative to the baseline.
The modified alloy will retain low hysteresis relative to the baseline.
The modified alloy will retain mechanical stability relative to the baseline.
The hypothesis applies only to an alloy-composition range having sufficient lattice distortion to enhance the magnetocaloric response.
The exact relationship among lattice distortion, magnetic-moment localization, and magnetocaloric response is undetermined.
Failure of magnetocaloric response to increase with increasing lattice distortion would falsify the hypothesis.
Significant degradation of heat-exchange rate, hysteresis-loop area, or mechanical stability with increasing lattice distortion would falsify the hypothesis.
